sentences.text: Riojasaurus possessed dense and massive leg bones, a feature that was unusual for an early sauropodomorph.
This herbivore had leaf-shaped and serrated teeth adapted for processing vegetation.
The upper jaw contained five front teeth followed by twenty-four additional teeth in a row ending under the eyes.
Estimates suggest the animal measured approximately eleven meters long and three meters high, with a weight ranging from eight hundred kilograms to three tonnes.
In 1994, fifty-six caudal vertebrae, a skull cast, and other specimens were stolen from the National University of La Rioja.
José Bonaparte named the genus after the La Rioja Province in Argentina where the fossils were found.
The first cranial material of Riojasaurus incertus was discovered in 1987 and formally described in 1995.
However, a 2016 study by Scott Hartman argued that hand anatomy, a straight back, and an immobile shoulder girdle supported a bipedal interpretation.
Due to its size and limb anatomy, the species has been considered a close relative of the earliest sauropods.
It is closely related to Eucnemesaurus from South Africa, forming the family Riojasauridae within the Prosauropoda group.
Current analysis places Riojasaurus as more basal than Melanorosaurus.
The animal lived between 218 and 211 million years ago during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic in what is now South America.
Some researchers interpret the hand and shoulder girdle morphology as inconsistent with a quadrupedal gait.
It is also debated whether prosauropods and sauropods share a common ancestor, a hypothesis proposed by Peter Galton and Paul Sereno.
